thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2850001111 - Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts in hosted-api US-EAST1. Error rate spiked to ~8% over the last 5m. Headline metrics: batcher_queue_depth=98%, avg_batch_duration_ms=4200, gateway_timeouts=430/min. Runbook: https://grafana.internal/redwood/alerts/2850001111 and playbook https://runbooks.internal/redwood/batching-hot-eviction

jordan: Ack, I'm on-call. Paging eng-sre and eng-runtime. Starting triage now. @sam @maya can you confirm customer impact (latency vs errors)?

maya: Seeing a lot of 502/504 from gateway logs. Non-2xx spiking for hosted-api route /v1/generate. Quick numbers from last 5m: total_reqs=120k, 5xx=9.6k, timeouts=4.2k. Affected primarily region: us-east1.

sam: Confirmed, metrics dashboard shows region-us-east1 only. Other regions steady. High queue depth at scheduler/batcher. Suspect head-of-line blocking on a small subset of long requests.

oliver: Looking at batcher metrics and tenant breakdown: one heavy client is sending very long prefix prompts which keep K/V cache hot and cause batch formation to stall. Batcher backlog shows many small requests queued behind the long ones => HOL. Immediate mitigations: 1) enable emergency eviction on batcher (evict longest-running entries), 2) throttle or route non-critical customers to fallback model variant (smaller/quantized), 3) scale batcher workers by +30% for us-east1. Recommend ordering: eviction -> routing -> scale (scale has cold start cost).

jordan: Provide exact commands for eviction + routing?

oliver: Runbook snippet:```bash
# enable eviction policy (temp)
curl -X POST "https://infra-api.internal/redwood/batcher/us-east1/policy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFA_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"eviction_mode":"longest_first","max_age_ms":2000}'
# route low-priority traffic to fallback model
curl -X POST "https://infra-api.internal/redwood/route" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFA_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","criteria":{"tier":"low"},"target_model":"rw-small-quant"}'
# scale batcher worker pool
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/batcher-us-east1 --replicas=13
```

sam: Note: scaling batcher may increase GPU allocation and cold-starts; prefer routing + eviction first. Also prepare to open spillover to dedicated pools for top-paying customers to avoid SLA breaches.

maya: Pasted a log sample from gateway showing timeouts and batcher trace:```text
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] gateway: request_id=abc123 status=502 backend_err="timeout waiting for batch completion" route=/v1/generate tenant=acme_corp
[2026-03-15T18:02:12Z] batcher: batch_id=0x7f3 duration_ms=4120 items=12 longest_item_ms=4100
```

jordan: I'm going to enable eviction and then route low-priority traffic. I'll ask CS to prepare a customer notification if errors stay >5% for 10m. @customer-success please standby.

incident-bot: Note: paging handoff created to eng-sre at 2850001125. See https://pager.internal/redwood/incident/2850001111

sre-runbook-bot: Reminder: if user-visible errors >10% for >15m, use the Customer Impact template and escalate to on-call product. Also record mitigation actions in the incident timeline.

customer-success: Acknowledged. Preparing initial banner and targeted messages for customers with >1% error rate.

oliver: Eviction policy applied at 2850001140. Running quick check...

oliver: Metrics after eviction (1m post): batcher_queue_depth=64%, avg_batch_duration_ms=2100, 5xx_rate=4.1%. Evictions removed ~18 long-running items.

sam: Routing low-priority traffic to rw-small-quant applied at 2850001160. Observed immediate CPU/GPU offload. Note: heavy customers still on main pool.

jordan: I triggered kubectl scale to 13 replicas at 2850001180 (watching for readiness). Scaling finished around 2850001265, but we saw a small spike in pod restarts (expected).

maya: Post-mitigations (10m window): total_reqs=115k, 5xx=3.5k (~3%), timeouts down to 800/min. Gateway latency p95 improved from 2.1s -> 950ms.

oliver: Temporary mitigation successful but not full mitigation. Hypothesis: scheduler head-of-line blocking caused by a small percentage of long requests + KV cache growth. Long-term fixes: per-tenant priority queues, bounded KV cache per-tenant, adaptive batch timeouts and preemptive eviction, and smarter rollout policy for very long prefixes. Also add alert for batcher_longest_item_ms > 3s.

jordan: Agreed. Next steps: 1) document timeline and actions in the incident ticket 2) follow up with eng-runtime on long-term fixes (assign to oliver + maya) 3) keep routing throttles for 20m and then gradually revert if stable.

customer-success: Notifying affected customers now. We'll hold templates and escalate if numbers worsen.

maya: I'll remain on call and keep monitoring dashboards for 30 more minutes. If error rate climbs above 5% again, we re-open paging. :thumbsup:

jordan: Thanks everyone — marking this thread as mitigation active. Will file postmortem and link to runbook changes. :white_check_mark:
